title: Groundwater depletion and aquifer monitoring
bottleneck: Agriculture uses about 70% of global freshwater, much of it from aquifers pumped faster than recharge — in India, 29% of groundwater blocks are overexploited, and complete loss of groundwater could cut the country's crop production by 28%. Yet pumping is largely unmonitored and unregulated: millions of private wells, no metering, subsidized electricity, no enforcement. You can't manage what you don't measure, and we don't measure it.
why_it_blocks: Aquifers are the buffer making dry-season farming possible. Depleting them converts productive farmland toward desert with no recovery on human timescales. Aquifers are the buffer making dry-season farming possible; depleting them converts farmland toward desert.
current_state: Satellite gravimetry maps depletion from orbit, but ground-level monitoring and regulation remain rare while depletion accelerates.
